subject: community-medicine
title: Modes of Transmission: Vehicle, Vector, Airborne and Direct Spread

steps.title: Direct transmission without an intermediary
steps.tx: **Direct transmission** passes the agent person to person without intermediates: direct contact including skin and sexual contact, droplet spread over short range, contact with soil, inoculation into skin or mucosa, and transplacental vertical passage. Each route names its own barrier: condoms, masks at close range, wound care, antenatal screening.
steps.say: No intermediary, no delay. Skin contact, short-range droplets, soil contact, direct inoculation and placental passage all qualify. Each route names its own barrier, from condoms to antenatal screening.

steps.title: Vehicle-borne: water and food carry the agent
steps.tx: **Vehicle-borne transmission** moves agents on inanimate vehicles, chiefly water and food, also blood, organs and tissues. Water carries typhoid, cholera, dysentery, hepatitis A and gastroenteritis; contaminated food explodes as point source outbreaks. Agents may multiply in the vehicle, as bacteria in milk, or merely ride it, and the dose received decides severity.
steps.say: Water and food do the travelling. Typhoid, cholera and hepatitis ride water; shared meals explode as point source outbreaks. Agents may multiply inside the vehicle or merely ride it, and swallowed dose shapes severity.

steps.title: Vector-borne: mechanical versus biological
steps.tx: **Vector-borne transmission** divides into mechanical carriage, where the insect merely transports the agent (flies on food), and biological transmission, where the agent develops or multiplies inside the vector before delivery. Biological forms split further: propagative (multiplication only), developmental (development only) and cyclo-developmental (both), the malaria pattern examiners quote.
steps.say: Insects carry two ways. Mechanical carriage is transport only, flies seeding food. Biological transmission transforms the agent inside the vector: multiplication alone, development alone, or both together as malaria shows. The distinction decides incubation inside the vector.

steps.tx: **Vector borne transmission** splits into mechanical carriage and biological transmission. In mechanical carriage the insect only transports the agent, as when flies seed food. In biological transmission the agent develops or multiplies inside the vector before the next delivery. Biological forms divide again into propagative spread, which is multiplication only, developmental spread, which is development only, and cyclo developmental spread, which is both. Malaria is the cyclo developmental pattern. That distinction is what creates an extrinsic incubation period inside the mosquito.
steps.say: Flies that merely drop organisms onto food are mechanical vectors. Biological vectors let the organism multiply, develop, or do both before the next bite. Malaria does both inside the mosquito. The time required for that internal change is the extrinsic incubation period.

vis.alt: A mosquito life cycle shows malaria parasites developing and multiplying inside the insect before the next bite.
vis.caption: Parasites enter the mosquito, mature, and increase in number before they can be delivered to another person. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Airborne: droplet nuclei travel far
steps.tx: **Droplet nuclei** are dried residues under 5 microns that float for hours and travel metres, carrying tuberculosis, measles and chickenpox beyond the index room. Larger droplets fall within about a metre and count as direct spread instead. Ventilation, upper-room air disinfection and respiratory isolation answer the nuclei; distance alone answers droplets.
steps.say: Size decides distance. Dried nuclei under five microns float for hours carrying tuberculosis and measles across rooms. Larger droplets fall within a metre. Ventilation answers nuclei; mere distance answers only droplets.

steps.tx: **Droplet nuclei** are dried residues under 5 microns that float for hours and travel metres, carrying tuberculosis, measles, and chickenpox beyond the index room. Larger droplets fall within about a metre and count as direct spread rather than airborne spread. Ventilation, disinfection of upper room air, and respiratory isolation answer the nuclei. Distance alone answers droplets. An instruction that only says stand one metre away does not control the infections that ride on the smaller, lingering particles.
steps.say: Dried residues under 5 microns stay aloft for hours and can carry tuberculosis, measles, and chickenpox across rooms. Larger droplets fall within about a metre and act as direct spread. Ventilation and respiratory isolation answer the nuclei. Distance alone answers only the large droplets.

vis.alt: A particle diagram compares droplet nuclei smaller than 5 microns, floating for hours, with large droplets that fall within one metre.
vis.caption: Tiny dried residues remain airborne across a room, while large respiratory droplets settle within about a metre of the source. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Fomites and unclean hands
steps.tx: **Fomite-borne spread** uses contaminated articles: towels, linen, utensils, toys and medical instruments bridging patients. Unclean hands and fingers deserve their own category in the classic scheme, seeding food and mucosa after toilet contact. Handwashing, instrument sterilisation and prompt refrigeration of prepared food cut this whole family at household level.
steps.say: Objects and hands bridge patients. Towels, utensils and instruments carry agents between hosts, and unclean fingers seed food after toilet contact. Handwashing and sterilisation cut the whole family at its cheapest point.

nodes.label: Susceptible touches, then mouth or wound

steps.title: Breaking the chain at its weakest link
steps.tx: **Interruption of transmission** changes the environment between reservoir and susceptible host: water treatment from chlorination to full processing, clean food practice, vector and breeding place destruction, and stray animal control. Droplet infections resist this link and lean instead on early treatment and hygiene of secretions, a contrast stems test directly.
steps.say: Attack the middle link environmentally. Treated water, clean food practice and vector destruction break chains before hosts meet agents. Droplet infections resist this link and lean on early treatment plus secretion hygiene instead.

rows: Water, food, vector and hand measures

steps.title: Protecting the susceptible host
steps.tx: The third link takes **active immunisation**, passive immunoglobulin for immediate cover, combined active-passive post-exposure care, chemoprophylaxis for defined exposures, and non-specific measures such as nutrition and personal protection. Diseases controlled solely by immunisation, polio, tetanus, diphtheria and measles among them, prove this link can carry an entire programme.
steps.say: Strengthen the final link. Vaccines for durable cover, immunoglobulin for immediate cover, both together after exposure, drugs for defined risks. Polio, tetanus, diphtheria and measles control rests almost entirely on this link.

steps.title: Matching route to disease in stems
steps.tx: Stems encode routes in clues: **well water plus monsoon flooding** suggests water-borne enteric disease, a shared wedding meal suggests food vehicle point source, and winter crowding with cough suggests droplet spread. Sexual contact, blood products and mosquito density each name their route. Read the clue before the organism; control marks follow the route, not the microbe name.
steps.say: Clues name routes before organisms. Flooded wells, shared meals, winter crowding, blood products, mosquito density: each points one way. Control answers follow the route identified, so decode the setting first.

steps.title: One Health closing note
steps.tx: **Zoonotic spillover** reminds planners that animal reservoirs, vectors and human behaviour meet in one system: destroying stray dogs, controlling cattle infection and managing rodent reservoirs protect people without a single human prescription. Transmission thinking therefore ends where this set began, with environment and society deciding which microbes reach susceptible hosts.
steps.say: Close the loop ecologically. Animal reservoirs, vectors and human behaviour form one system, so dog, cattle and rodent measures protect people without prescriptions. Transmission answers live in environments and societies, not microbes alone.
